key_insight: OpenSeeker fully open-sources the training data, tooling, and baselines needed to build frontier search-capable LLM agents, removing the primary data barrier that has kept this capability inside a few companies.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of transparent, high-quality training data and reproducible pipelines for training search agents, which has limited academic and community innovation in search-enabled LLM agents.
method: Curate and release a large, structured dataset of search interactions (queries, retrieval traces, tool calls, and agent reasoning) designed for training search agents.
Provide standardized annotation schemas, training/fine-tuning recipes, and evaluation benchmarks to enable reproducible model development.
Open-source baseline agent implementations and the end-to-end pipeline under a permissive license to encourage community adoption and extension.
impact: By democratizing access to the data and code required to train search agents, OpenSeeker enables researchers and practitioners to reproduce, improve, and compete with industrial systems—accelerating innovation and lowering barriers to entry.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: user query → web retrieval → agent reasoning & tool calls → final answer
Dataset composition graphic: proportions of queries, retrieval traces, tool interactions, and human annotations
Benchmark chart: baseline OpenSeeker agents vs closed-source baselines on key search-agent tasks
Open-source/community iconography: download, license, and contribution flow to show accessibility
paper_title: OpenSeeker: Democratizing Frontier Search Agents by Fully Open-Sourcing Training Data
paper_authors: Yuwen Du, Rui Ye, Shuo Tang, Xinyu Zhu, Yijun Lu
